Wealth Platform · Journey Layer · Flowcharting Exercise

V1 Journey Flowcharts

The core functional journeys, human and non-human, drawn at spine altitude and reconciled against the five entity references, the J-docs, the four V1 core docs, and the Open Decisions Register v0.15. Each diagram is paired with a prose outline, a scenarios block, and the canon-reconciliation seam.

StatusFirst full pass · 17 of 17 drawn
DateJune 2026
SourceFunctional dump, reconciled to canon
FormatA3 landscape, print-ready
SegmentMass affluent, Tier 2, MFD

The functional dump re-cuts the underlying J-docs rather than mirroring them one to one, so several journeys fuse multiple canon flows and five of the twelve investor-facing journeys are recommendation- or nudge-shaped. Each journey is drawn at a governing spine altitude: the canonical happy path, the genuine forks, and the ways it terminates short of success. Where a journey fuses canon, crosses a still-open decision, or sits on the MFD dissection-not-prescription boundary, that seam is marked on the flow rather than buried in prose.

How to read this deck

Part A is the human journeys, an investor at the keyboard. Part B is the non-human journeys, the engines and pipes that run with no investor present. The compliance boundary on the recommendation- and nudge-shaped surfaces is drawn as an in-flow gate, with the open policing-chokepoint decision shown as a governing dependency, because that boundary is the spine of nearly half the human set, not a footnote.

Conventions

Human journey: investor at the keyboard Non-Human journey: engine or pipe, no investor present
COMPLIANCE on the MFD dissection-not-prescription boundary   OPEN a node rests on a register decision still open   FUSION fuses or re-cuts canon J-docs   NO J-DOC entities and core docs only, no dedicated J-doc behind it

Part AHuman journeys

J1 · First-time experience and successful KYC Human

FUSION J1 and J2 together re-cut canon J1, split at the DigiLocker-found fork.

Journey outline

The front door for a returning or net-new mass-affluent investor. They land on a homepage built to carry trust markers and the wealth-creation framing, then authenticate with a mobile-number OTP. Social login, where offered, is an identity hint and a convenience, never a KYC source. The platform then attempts a DigiLocker, CKYC, or KRA fetch against the identity rail.

This is the happy path: the fetch returns an existing record. If it is already Validated, the verify step collapses to a fetch-and-confirm and the investor reaches a transactable identity in one move. If it returns only Registered, a single incremental Aadhaar-validation step lifts it to Validated, the only status that clears a new fund house. From there the investor flows into J3 activation. When the fetch finds nothing, control hands to J2 for a fresh KYC.

Key scenarios

  • Fetch returns Validated. The clean case. Fetch-and-confirm, straight to transactable.
  • Fetch returns Registered. Not a failure, but not enough for a new fund house. Incremental Aadhaar validation before any first order can route.
  • Fetch returns nothing. Deterministic handoff to J2, so the fresh-KYC persona depth lives in one place.
  • Inoperative PAN. A pre-condition, not a post-submission surprise: the record drops to a blocked state and must be made operative first. Drawn as a side-exit.
  • Social login present. Bulleted, not branched: it changes the sign-in convenience, not the KYC path.

Reconciliation notes

Maps to the capture-and-fetch front half of canon J1. The DigiLocker step is canon's CKYC / KRA fetch modality. The Validated versus Registered distinction and the "only Validated clears a new fund house" red flag carry verbatim from J1. Joint, NRI, and Minor depth is held for J2. No open decisions touched.

J2 · Needs fresh KYC: persona handling and eSign Human

FUSION The persona depth of canon J1, entered when J1's fetch finds no record.

Journey outline

The fresh-KYC path, reached when no record exists to fetch. After OTP login the investor lands on the homepage and into a KYC request block, and the persona determines the route. Each of the three V1 personas changes the documents, the accounts, and the verification enough to be a genuine reroute, not just an added check. The verification uses a full-KYC modality, Video IPV or Biometric Aadhaar, because OTP-only eKYC carries a fifty-thousand-rupee per fund house ceiling that breaks immediately at affluent ticket sizes. The investor eSigns, and the record resolves to Validated (or to Registered with an Aadhaar-validation step that lifts it) before flowing into J3.

Key scenarios

  • Joint is an overlay, not a branch. Applied over any natural persona; each holder is KYC'd individually, and single-holder OTP eKYC is excluded, so a joint holding forces full KYC. Bulleted, not drawn.
  • NRI / OCI refusals. A US or Canada resident refused by the AMC over FATCA and PFIC burden, missing overseas address proof, a foreign-number validation gap, or an unmet Aadhaar-linkage requirement for capital-market products. Route to an accepting AMC, complete proofs, validate by email, link Aadhaar.
  • Minor. The minor's record cannot stand alone; complete the guardian's full KYC and the relationship evidence.
  • PoA-operated NRI. An authority overlay captured at onboarding, not a separate path. The PoA holder cannot later nominate, but that is J10's concern.
  • Foreign National resident. A narrow natural persona surfaced as a scope question, not drawn as a governing branch.

Reconciliation notes

This is canon J1's persona section, drawn as its own functional journey. The "only Validated clears a new fund house" bar is sharper for non-residents since the cross-fund-house relaxation lapsed on 30 April 2026 (D2, applied as settled). Entity personas (HUF, non-individuals) are an explicit deferral to Private Wealth and out of V1.

J3 · Activation: accounts, penny-drop, eligibility, risk, RM Human

FUSION NO J-DOC J1's tail plus net-new steps (risk profiling, RM mapping) that no J-doc owns yet.

Journey outline

The convergence step both KYC personas land on. With a transactable identity established, the platform fetches the investor's bank account and verifies it with a penny-drop, the cheapest place to catch a wrong or mismatched account before any money is in motion. It then resolves instrument eligibility (in V1 that is materially mutual funds; direct equity is a V1.5 instrument), captures a risk profile that feeds suitability, and maps the investor to a relationship manager. Past these, the investor is activated and ready to invest.

Key scenarios

  • Penny-drop mismatch. Name or account validation fails; loop back to re-verify or re-enter rather than proceed on a bad account.
  • Equity eligibility. Shown as a node but deferred: direct equity is V1.5, so V1 eligibility resolves to MF plus persona constraints.
  • RM book-valuation basis. The single most consequential incentive decision: the mapping should tie to goal fulfillment, not AUM. Noted as a design constraint on the RM step.
  • Risk profile. Captured here, consumed later by suitability gates in the order pre-flight.

Canon gap, flagged honestly

Penny-drop and instrument eligibility reconcile cleanly against the Investor and Instruments references and the Rails identity path. Risk profiling and RM relationship mapping have no dedicated J-doc; they are drawn against the Relationships domain and the suitability posture in the core docs and are the most interpretive part of this diagram. Worth a dedicated J-doc before this hardens into a build contract.

J4 · Portfolio Review: held-away aggregation and dissection Split

COMPLIANCE OPEN Cert-gated on Sahamati; dissection-only; D49 tax display open. The AA pull and refresh are the non-human half.

Journey outline

The consent-based held-away view, with the firm acting as a Financial Information User. The investor opts in, the firm raises a consent request that sets the entire scope (purpose, FI types, duration, fetch frequency, data range), and the investor grants it at their own Account Aggregator. On grant, the AA rail orchestrates a pull from the holding institutions through a blind pipe it cannot itself read. The platform composes a net-worth view, own book plus held-away, and everything it surfaces passes the dissection boundary before presentation: it states characteristics and a generic benchmark comparison, never a judgment. The consent then has a standing life of scheduled and on-demand refreshes, which is the non-human half handed to the engine.

Key scenarios

  • Declined or partial consent. Does not break the picture, it narrows it: show the own book plus whatever was shared and name the held-away gap honestly rather than imply completeness.
  • Refresh cadence. Monthly scheduled, on-demand when frequency cap and latency allow, otherwise serve the last pull with an honest as-of stamp.
  • Revoke. Withdrawal is the only write besides the consent itself; revoking loops into J12 preferences.
  • Tax display. Indicative and clearly disclaimed in V1 because the platform holds no cost basis (D49 open).

Two seams drawn into the flow

Cert-gated: the whole journey gates on Sahamati certification and is the designated drop-if-slips element if it does not land by go-live. J4 vs J9: this journey is the held-away picture via AA; the investor's own on-platform holdings are J9's "My Portfolio". The dissection-only posture is identical across both, but the data source and the cert dependency are not.

J5 · Goals: templated and custom Human

COMPLIANCE OPEN NO J-DOC The most compliance-loaded surface in V1: allocation guidance inside the MFD-incidental envelope.

Journey outline

Goal is the organising entity of the differentiating layer, not a feature bolted on. The investor picks one of three templates (First Crore, Home, Retirement) or defines a custom goal, then articulates a target amount and horizon. A forward projection makes the goal concrete, and the allocation-guidance step bridges from intent to instrument. That bridge is the most compliance-loaded surface in V1: it sits inside the MFD-incidental envelope, is built for the conservative case while the SEBI MFD-RIA boundary is under live review, and clears a strict Compliance gate. A created goal renders holdings beneath it, the investor can add more, and funding a goal routes into J8.

Key scenarios

  • Forward projection. Long-horizon projections (a 25-year retirement curve) are the highest-risk element here; they must read as illustrative, not as a promise or a recommendation.
  • Allocation guidance. MFD-incidental, never advice-for-fee. Anything that cannot stay factual is reframed or suppressed at the gate.
  • Add more goals. The multi-goal case is the bet: not whether goals exist, but whether users personalise and fund them.

Open decision drawn into the flow

The Goal Engine is one of the recommendation-shaped surfaces whose policing is an open structural decision, unresolved as of Architecture View v0.3 and gating PRDs 2, 4, and 6. There is no dedicated J-doc behind Goals; this is drawn from the Goal Engine domain and the MFD posture in the core docs.

J6 · Discovery: browse, filter, sort, pills Human

COMPLIANCE OPEN NO J-DOC Canon splits this: objective browse is safe, the governed ranking console is supervised.

Journey outline

The query surface that composes Catalog, Scheme Intelligence, and the Portfolio overlay into something an investor browses. Canon splits it deliberately. Objective browse, filter, and sort is safe and carries no compliance load. Characteristic pills surface facts and are read-only, owning no state. The governed ranking console is where business intervention is allowed but supervised, and everything it emits must pass the dissection gate before it shows. From a selection the investor routes into a transaction, or into the J7 basket overlay if they want something curated.

Key scenarios

  • Objective vs governed. Browse and sort need no gate. The ranking console does, because business curation can read as a recommendation.
  • Pills. Factual characteristics only ("top-quartile 3-year return", "expense ratio X"), never a prompt to act.
  • Hand-off to J7. When the investor wants a basket rather than a single scheme, Discovery routes into the recommendation overlay, which carries its own heavier gates.

Reconciliation notes

No dedicated J-doc; drawn from the Discovery read layer and the Catalog and Scheme Intelligence domains. Pills are one of the three recommendation-shaped surfaces under the open policing decision. The split between the safe objective surface and the supervised governed console is the load-bearing distinction and is drawn, not bulleted.

J7 · Recommendation overlay: cohort baskets and alternatives Human

COMPLIANCE OPEN NO J-DOC Policing mechanism unresolved as of Architecture View v0.3.

Journey outline

The investor enters a curated surface: pre-configured baskets assembled at cohort level, not as personalised advice, with alternative funds shown alongside. Everything the surface emits passes two gates before the screen. The dissection boundary is first: the surface may state a characteristic but never judge or prescribe; anything reading as advice is reframed to factual or suppressed. The Compliance gate is second: the whole surface sits inside the MFD-incidental envelope and is built for the conservative case. Only what clears both gates is presented, disclaimers attached. A selection routes into J8; otherwise no action is recorded.

Key scenarios

  • Alternative funds. Switch-nudge-adjacent and the single highest-risk element. A comparison is permissible; a prompt to switch is not.
  • Cohort vs individual. Baskets are cohort-level by construction. The moment one becomes individually tailored it crosses toward advice, out of posture. The "not personalised" label is load-bearing.
  • Gate fails. Content that cannot be made factual is suppressed, not softened.
  • Disclaimers. A check on the present step, noted rather than branched.

Open decision drawn into the flow

The recommendation-shaped surfaces can each read as recommendation-shaped. Whether they police the dissection boundary independently or route through one shared enforcement chokepoint is a structural decision, unresolved as of v0.3, and it gates PRDs 2, 4, and 6. The POL node marks exactly where that decision lands.

J9 · Folio and My Portfolio Human

FUSION COMPLIANCE Canon J3 (folio) plus the on-platform Portfolio Service read. Distinct from J4's held-away view.

Journey outline

Two things under one roof: the folio container coming into being, and the My Portfolio read over what it holds. A folio does not exist until a first transaction into a fund house brings it into being, since the RTA issues the number on first transaction. So the spine starts from a holding intent, checks reuse-or-create, shapes the container (SOA form, operation mode, repatriability tag, nomination), and goes Active carrying its first holding. The My Portfolio view then renders the investor's on-platform holdings under their goals, and like every portfolio surface it is dissection-only: value, XIRR, overlap, concentration, cap split, with any benchmark comparison disclaimed.

Key scenarios

  • Reuse. When a folio for this investor, AMC, mode, and repatriability exists, the holding lands in it and the container step is a no-op. Guards against duplicate-folio fragmentation.
  • Legitimate multiple folios. Different modes or repatriability classes correctly produce separate folios with the same AMC; the reuse check guards only same-mode duplicates.
  • Nomination gate. A single-holder folio must nominate or formally opt out at creation; the standing life of that nomination is J10.
  • Mode / repatriability mismatch. A repatriable folio funded from a non-repatriable account is blocked before registration.

Reconciliation notes

Folio creation reconciles to canon J3 (SOA-only in V1, no demat fork). The My Portfolio read is the Portfolio Service dissection overlay. This is the on-platform counterpart to J4: same dissection posture, different data source, no AA dependency and no cert gate.

J10 · Nomination: mandatory, inline to transaction Human

FUSION Canon J4 nomination. D10 settled at three nominees; D12 freeze boundary drawn.

Journey outline

A nomination is an instruction against a folio, not an order, with no money leg. It is mandatory at folio creation and editable thereafter. The flow has two heavy gates and a long shadow. The timing gate comes first: a nomination cannot change once a death has been intimated, because survivorship or transmission has taken over and a change would route units to the wrong person. The authority gate is second: only the investor may nominate, never a PoA holder, and a joint folio needs every holder's consent regardless of operation mode. Past both, the capture is light (name and relationship mandatory, up to three nominees, shares totalling the whole or split equally), registered with the RTA folio by folio.

Key scenarios

  • Death intimated. The nomination freezes and the folio routes to transmission. This is the hard boundary with the servicing layer.
  • PoA cannot nominate. Void no matter how clean the data.
  • Joint consent. Even an either-or-survivor folio cannot have its nominee changed by one holder alone.
  • Presentation red flag. The place an investor edits a nomination is where the platform is tempted to misdescribe what a nominee is. A nominee is a receiver of custody, not an heir; survivorship is not estate planning. The copy must not imply otherwise.

Reconciliation notes

Reconciles to canon J4. D10 is settled by the 29 May 2026 SEBI circular (maximum three nominees, effective 1 September 2026), so the capture form builds to three with a residual Compliance confirmation against the primary circular text. "Part of transaction" in the dump means the creation-time gate is inline; this journey owns the standing edits.

J11 · Redemption: assess, caution or celebrate, redeem Human

COMPLIANCE OPEN The caution-or-celebrate nudge is the compliance-sensitive surface; D45 NRI pre-trade visibility open.

Journey outline

Money out, one scheme, no payment mandate. The assess step runs the pre-flight gates money-out carries (unencumbered units, lock-in elapsed, KYC valid) and surfaces the factual consequences of redeeming now: exit-load haircut, short- or long-term capital-gains treatment, and progress against the goal the holding sits under. That is the caution-or-celebrate moment, and it must stay factual. The order then runs the redemption spine to Allotted, where residential status forks the payout: a resident receives full proceeds, an NRI or OCI has capital-gains TDS withheld at source and the net routed by repatriability. Settlement is handed to the Recon journey.

Key scenarios

  • Caution or celebrate. A behavioural-nudge surface close to the MFD boundary. "Redeeming now incurs exit load X and STCG Y; you are Z percent toward your goal" is dissection. "You should not sell" is prescription and out of posture.
  • NRI TDS fork. The signature of the journey: the same event produces a different obligation by a single attribute, then repatriability decides where proceeds land.
  • No cost basis in V1. The firm reflects the gain and TDS the AMC and RTA compute; it does not compute them itself (D45 open for NRI pre-trade net visibility).
  • Failed vs Reversed. Inherited from the order spine; the unwind lives with Recon.

Reconciliation notes

Reconciles to canon J9. The dump's "assess, caution or celebrate, redeem" maps onto the pre-flight gates, the nudge surface, and the redemption spine. The nudge is the new compliance-sensitive element the functional framing introduces, drawn with an explicit factual-only gate.

J12 · User Preferences: consent, comms, RM Human

NO J-DOC The Consent and Authorization domain plus Relationships. Consent here is legally operative.

Journey outline

The investor's control surface over consent, communications, and their relationship. Consent is the heavy part: DPDP processing consent, the view-and-revoke of AA consents, and mandate authorization are binding, non-repudiable artifacts with their own lifecycle, retention, and audit trail, not mere settings. Communications preferences govern channels and frequency. The relationship area lets the investor view or request an RM. Everything persists as an auditable artifact and reflects across surfaces; revoking an AA consent loops back into J4's standing life.

Key scenarios

  • Consent is legally operative. Treated as a ledger of artifacts, not toggles; each carries purpose limitation and a retention shadow.
  • AA revoke. Stops future held-away pulls and loops to J4, where the picture narrows to the own book.
  • RM flows. Drawn from the Relationships domain; the RM-facing workstation is post-V1, but the relationship mapping is V1.

Canon gap, flagged honestly

No dedicated J-doc. Drawn from the Consent and Authorization cross-cutting domain (AA, NACH/mandate, KYC and DPDP consent) and the Relationships domain. The consent half is well-grounded in the core docs; the comms and RM halves are the more interpretive parts and would benefit from a J-doc before build.

Part BNon-Human journeys

J8 · Transaction and the order state machine Non-Human

FUSION Canon J6, the most-reused spine. Cut at Allotted; the settled tail is owned by Recon.

Journey outline

The canonical single-order lifecycle every transaction journey instantiates, routed through FP. An order arrives Placed once intent is validated (authority, eligibility, KYC, suitability, cut-off, and the direction gate), then passes one pre-flight gate; every failed check sends it to Failed with no money moved, which is why the gate is one node, not a row of forks. The single genuine fork is direction: money in initiates a non-pooled payment leg and prices on funds realisation; money out registers a redemption with no money leg. Both reach Allotted, where, per the functional cut, the journey hands off; Settled and Reversed are owned by Recon. Money never passes through the firm.

Key scenarios

  • Retries and idempotency. Within-state behaviour on the routed and acknowledged legs; re-attempts a step rather than rerouting the spine.
  • State propagation. Each transition emits a domain event onto the spine; downstream reads are projections, not part of this flow.
  • Failed vs Reversed. Failed is pre-settlement with nothing to unwind; Reversed is a post-allotment unwind and lives with Recon.
  • NAV timing. A purchase placed before cut-off but funded a day later takes the later day's NAV. A pricing input noted on the acknowledged step.

Reconciliation notes

Canon J6 drawn rail-agnostic with FP as the V1 rail. The one deliberate deviation is yours: J6 owns the full Placed to Settled spine, but the functional cut stops at Allotted and routes settlement into Recon. The handoff node makes that seam explicit so neither flow silently owns the other.

S1 · Ledger Non-Human

NO J-DOC Spec 2 territory. A reconciliation projection of RTA truth, never the system of record.

Journey outline

An engine, not a screen. The ledger subscribes to the domain event spine and writes double-entry, bitemporal, immutable postings. It is a projection of folio and unit truth that the Recon journey reconciles against the RTA feed. Two architectural constraints define it: no money ever transits the platform, because under the MFD posture the firm never pools client money, and there is no advisory-fee posting, because the firm charges none. The ledger is the moat that never shows in a feature comparison: it is what lets the platform answer arbitrary questions about past state and reconcile cleanly.

Key scenarios

  • Bitemporal. Both valid-time and transaction-time are kept, so the books can answer "what did we believe, and when" as well as "what was true".
  • Projection, not SoR. The RTA register is the truth; the ledger is a reconciled reflection. It never overrides the RTA.
  • No advisory-fee posting. A direct consequence of the MFD-not-RIA posture, carried as a ledger invariant.

Reconciliation notes

Drawn from the core-doc treatment of the canonical ledger; the underlying Spec is in flux and slated for a rewrite, so the concept is drawn (reconciliation projection, no-pooling, no advisory-fee posting) rather than any specific posting schema.

S2 · Recon: RTA reconciliation Non-Human

NO J-DOC Owns the Allotted to Settled tail that J8 and J11 hand off.

Journey outline

The engine that closes the order lifecycle. It takes the handoff from J8 and J11 at Allotted, ingests the RTA feed (CAMS and KFin mailback and CAS), and matches the platform's projection against the RTA truth. A clean match emits Settled; a dishonour or post-allotment error emits Reversed; a mismatch goes to an exception queue for manual reconciliation. This is where the settled and reversed terminals that J8 deliberately did not own actually resolve. In V1 reconciliation is batch; microbatch is a V2 upgrade.

Key scenarios

  • Settled. The projection agrees with the RTA register; units are on the register and payment realised, or proceeds have reached the bank.
  • Reversed. A post-allotment unwind; the order spine's reversed edge resolves here, not in J8.
  • Break. A mismatch the match cannot resolve goes to an exception queue rather than silently settling.
  • Cadence. Batch in V1; the move to microbatch is a deliberate V2 item.

Reconciliation notes

This journey exists because the functional cut split J6's tail. It is the natural home for the settled and reversed terminals and for the RTA reconciliation the ledger projects against. No dedicated J-doc; drawn from the Ledger and Reconciliation treatment in the core docs.

S3 · Data Lake Non-Human

NO J-DOC Analytical sink. Clickstream stays permanently separate from the domain event spine.

Journey outline

The analytical sink. It consumes domain events off the spine and, separately, behavioural clickstream events off their own plane. The load-bearing rule is the separation: the clickstream plane and the domain event spine are kept permanently distinct, so behavioural data never contaminates the system-of-record-grade event flow and vice versa. The lake feeds the Analytics and Reports journey downstream.

Key scenarios

  • Two planes in, kept apart. Domain events and clickstream both land in the lake but are never merged upstream of it.
  • Sink, not source. The lake derives from the spine; it is not a system of record and emits nothing back onto the spine.
  • Consent shadow. Behavioural capture carries a purpose-limitation and consent shadow even when nothing surfaces.

Reconciliation notes

No dedicated J-doc; drawn from the architecture treatment of the spine, the clickstream plane, and the analytical sink. The permanent clickstream-vs-spine separation is a locked principle and is drawn as the governing boundary.

S4 · CRM Sync Non-Human

NO J-DOC V1 is a legacy-adapter push. An ACL, not a relationships concern. Distinct from the BAU CRM build.

Journey outline

The narrowest of the system journeys in V1, and deliberately so. The relationship substrate (the commercial-relationship graph and the nominee-and-inferred-family graph, plus referral, children, and household) is built in V1 even though the RM-facing surface is not. In V1 that substrate ingests outbound into the legacy CRM through a single adapter sitting behind the anti-corruption layer. It is an integration edge, not a relationships feature, and the core never takes the CRM's shape.

Key scenarios

  • Outbound only in V1. Domain info pushes into the legacy CRM; this is a sync edge, not a two-way integration.
  • ACL discipline. One adapter per domain; the core stays swappable when the CRM changes.
  • Not the BAU CRM. Per your confirmation, this is the legacy-adapter push from the V1 platform, separate from the BAU pod's CRM initiative.

Reconciliation notes

Drawn from the Legacy CRM Sync block in the core docs (an outbound integration edge, an ACL, not a relationships concern). Confirmed scope: V1 is the legacy-adapter push, not a CRM build.

S5 · Analytics and Reports Non-Human

NO J-DOC Reporting projections. Household roll-up is a reporting altitude, never a posting altitude.

Journey outline

The reporting layer over the lake. It builds reporting projections that drive investor and operations reports and analytics. The one thing to get right structurally is the household roll-up: it is a reporting projection, a way of presenting several investors together, and it is never a posting altitude in the ledger. Wrapping this layer, as it wraps every layer, is Audit and Attribution: ARN and EUIN attribution integrity on the order path, and a recommendation-surface audit trail that gives the MFD posture its provability.

Key scenarios

  • Household roll-up. A reporting construct only. It never becomes a ledger posting level, which would corrupt the books.
  • Attribution. ARN and EUIN integrity is carried through the order path so commissions and provenance are auditable.
  • Recommendation-surface trail. The audit trail that lets the firm prove a recommendation-shaped surface stayed inside dissection bounds.

Reconciliation notes

No dedicated J-doc; drawn from the reporting-projection treatment and the cross-cutting Audit and Attribution capability in the core docs. The household-as-reporting-projection rule is a locked principle and is drawn as such.

Document control. V1 Journey Flowcharts, first full pass, June 2026. All seventeen functional journeys drawn at spine altitude across two sections, human and non-human, reconciled against the five entity references, the J-docs, the four V1 core docs, and the Open Decisions Register v0.15. The functional dump re-cuts the J-docs where it does; fusions, open decisions (D45, D49, recommendation-surface policing), the Sahamati cert gate, and the MFD dissection-not-prescription boundaries are marked on the flows. Four journeys carry no dedicated J-doc (J3 risk and RM, J5 Goals, J6 Discovery, J12 Preferences, and the five system journeys) and are drawn from the entities and core docs, flagged accordingly. Approach, depth, the compliance-node treatment, the J8 settled-tail handoff, the J4 versus J9 split, and the CRM legacy-adapter scope are all confirmed.
